content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"FULL","rationale":"The book's core claim — that righteousness denotes right-living (conformity to God's ways, which for creatures means doing His commandments), received by grace but never redefined as a mere status detached from conduct — is directly stated by its cited texts rather than inferred from them. Deuteronomy 6:25 ('it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments') and Psalm 119:172 ('all thy commandments are righteousness') define the term as commandment-keeping in so many words; 1 John 3:7 explicitly forecloses the status-without-doing reading ('he that doeth righteousness is righteous'); Deuteronomy 32:4 and Psalm 145:17 ground the definition in God's own case (His ways and works are the measure of right). The book also does what a persuasive divergent reading must do: it answers the strongest counter-texts on their own terms. Romans 4:4 defines the excluded 'work' as a wage-claim creating debt, and Romans 4:7-8 explains the reckoning mechanism as forgiveness and covering of sin — not a renaming of wrong-living as right — which is precisely what the passage itself says via David's psalm. Philippians 3:9 is shown to contrast source and claim (mine-by-debt vs. God's-by-faith), not right-living vs. lawlessness, and Paul's immediate 'let us walk by the same rule' (3:16) supports that. The Revelation 19:8 lexical point is decisive for the garment symbol: dikaiōmata is plural and active ('righteous acts of the saints,' as ASV/ESV/NASB/NIV render it), while simultaneously being 'given unto her' — matching the book's 'granted, then worn' grammar and undercutting the common picture of the garment as pure imputed status. The forensic counter-reading must either bifurcate the term into unrelated senses or strain against Deut 6:25, Ps 119:172, 1 John 3:7, Rev 19:8, Rev 3:4, and Rev 22:14; it identifies no supplied text the book's core cannot explain without contradiction.","book_core_identification":"Righteousness is right-living: conformity to God's own ways and works, which are the measure of right; for those under His authority it is concretely the doing of His commandments. It is received and reckoned by grace through faith (via forgiveness, not wage-debt), but the gracious reckoning never converts righteousness into a bare status that renames wrong-living right.","book_secondary_elaborations":["The garment/robe symbolism: righteousness worn as clothing, with Rev 19:8's fine linen being righteous acts (dikaiōmata) — given by God yet put on by the saints","The bath-vs-feet-washing distinction (John 13): one baptismal covering, ongoing cleansing of conduct","The covenant framing: the garment as 'the covenant worn' (Ezekiel 16 skirt-spreading; kanaph/fringe imagery)","The reinterpretation of Isaiah 64:6 filthy rags as deeds stained by the doer's sin rather than obedience itself being filth","The armor-of-God derivation (Isaiah 59:17 as God's own war-dress, helmet of yeshuah)","The fig-leaf/self-made-covering contrast as the opposite error"],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"The classic forensic/imputed reading: in its theologically decisive (Pauline, soteriological) use, righteousness denotes a legal standing before God — Christ's righteousness credited to the believer's account through faith, apart from works (Rom 4:5-6; Phil 3:9; 2 Cor 5:21). The garment imagery (Isa 61:10; Zech 3:4) pictures this alien, bestowed status covering the sinner; ethical uprightness is a fruit of the status, not the referent of the term. Deut 6:25, Ps 119:172, and 1 John 3:7 belong to a distinct 'ethical' sense of the word that does not control the justification texts.","counter_core_identification":"Saving righteousness is a declared/credited legal status (right standing before God), constituted by imputation of Christ's righteousness rather than by any right-living of the person, with lived uprightness being a separate, derivative sense of the term.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"CONTRADICTS","material_core_denial":"The counter denies that righteousness is substantively right-living: it asserts that in the governing texts (Rom 4; Phil 3:9) righteousness names a status a person has, not something a person does, so that a man with no righteous living can be fully righteous in the term's primary sense. The book asserts the reverse: the term always means right-living; grace answers how a sinner receives it (forgiveness, faith reckoned), never what it is. Both cannot be true of the same referent.","counter_case":["Romans 4:5-6: God 'justifieth the ungodly' and 'imputeth righteousness without works' — righteousness is reckoned to someone precisely characterized as not working, suggesting a status not constituted by conduct","Philippians 3:9: Paul renounces 'mine own righteousness' for 'the righteousness which is of God by faith' — read as an alien righteousness replacing his own doing","Isaiah 64:6: 'all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags' — read as disqualifying human right-living from ever constituting righteousness before God","Isaiah 61:10 / Zech 3:4: the robe is bestowed and the filthy garments exchanged by God's act, suggesting the covering is given status rather than performed deeds","The KJV rendering of Rev 19:8 ('the righteousness of saints') supports the garment-as-status picture"],"book_explanatory_advantages":["Deut 6:25 and Ps 119:172 are explicit definitional statements equating righteousness with observing the commandments — the counter must quarantine these as a 'different sense' with no textual signal for the bifurcation","1 John 3:7 is a direct apostolic warning against the exact move the counter makes ('let no man deceive you: he that doeth righteousness is righteous'), which the book takes at face value and the counter must soften","Rev 19:8's Greek dikaiōmata (plural, 'righteous acts') with 'was given unto her' captures both the gift and the deed in one verse, exactly matching the book's 'granted, then worn' — the status-only reading depends on the narrowed KJV rendering","The book explains the reckoning mechanism from within Rom 4 itself: v.4 defines the excluded work as debt-claim, vv.7-8 define the imputation as forgiveness/covering of sin — no imported doctrine of transferred merit is needed","Deut 32:4 and Ps 145:17 give a unified definition covering God's own righteousness (His ways and works), which a forensic-status definition cannot do — God's righteousness is not a credited standing","The garment-maintenance texts (Rev 3:4 'not defiled their garments'; Rev 16:15 'keepeth his garments'; Jude 23; Rev 22:14) require the garment to be conduct preserving both the verse and Isaiah 1:16-18's command to wash and do right","Consistency with accepted prior premises: belief, faith, and love were each adjudicated as obedience-constitutive covenant
